F01.P1.justification: const n: i32 = 7; return n; — immutable binding, no annotation needed beyond literal typing.

F01.P2.fragment:
var counter: i64 = 0;
const LIMIT: i64 = 100;
F01.P2.justification: var counter: i64 = 0; const LIMIT: i64 = 100; at file scope — mutable var vs immutable const clearly distinguished.

F02.P1.justification: var v: i32 = undefined; then definite assignment on both branches of an if; Zig's `undefined` is the documented explicit uninitialized-storage marker satisfying R9's non-placeholder requirement (uninitialized is a first-class concept, not a hidden zero-fill).

F02.P2.justification: var buf: [16]u8 = undefined; — genuinely uninitialized buffer, documented Zig mechanism distinct from zero-init.

F03.P1.justification: x += 1; — compound assignment, checked-overflow in ReleaseSafe (ub/trap semantics documented).

F03.P2.justification: xs.items[1] = 42; on std.ArrayList(i32) mutates backing slice in place.

F04.P1.justification: const port = &slot; port.* = 9; — explicit pointer alias with write-through, dereference required by syntax.

F04.P2.justification: const window = xs.items[0..]; — non-copying slice view over existing storage; slices are documented as non-owning views.

F04.P3.justification: Pointer/reference equality via `==` on pointers to a heap-allocated struct — distinguishes identity from value equality; routing through a one-element array-list and reading back preserves the pointer for the identity test.

F05.P1.justification: f(x) bare call — Zig has no implicit reference passing for aggregate value types at an ordinary call site; ArrayList passed by value is a struct copy of the descriptor, elements are heap-shared depending on type, expressible and buildable.

F05.P2.justification: fn put(cell: *i32) void { cell.* = 12; } — explicit pointer parameter required by the language for caller-writable scalar access.

F05.P3.justification: Zig has no lexical closures: a nested function cannot capture a variable (`k`) from its enclosing function scope; only top-level/comptime-parameterized functions exist, and capturing state requires passing it explicitly as an argument/struct field, which the canonical_task's numbered sub-requirement (2) explicitly forbids (capture, not parameter passing). No documented mechanism satisfies sub-requirement (1); citation: Zig language reference, functions section — no closures/anonymous capturing functions are supported.

F06.P1.justification: fn mid(xs: []const i32) i32 { return xs[1]; } — returns a value (i32), independent of the slice, buildable.

F06.P2.justification: Zig supports returning an anonymous struct/tuple-like aggregate: fn divmod2(a,b: i32) struct{q:i32,r:i32} — destructure at call site.

F07.P1.justification: const r = a * b + c; ordinary precedence, checked-overflow semantics under ReleaseSafe.

F07.P2.justification: Zig requires explicit @divTrunc/@mod builtins for integer division/remainder (no bare `/` on ints without exactness guarantee) and @as(f64,...) conversions for float division — all explicit, buildable.

F08.P1.justification: @addWithOverflow(m, 1) returns a struct with overflow flag (rung akin to (i), substituting 0 on overflow) — behavior fully determinable from the construct; ReleaseSafe plain `+` traps deterministically as a fallback rung (iv).

F08.P2.fragment: const q: i32 = if (b == 0) 0 else @divTrunc(a, b);
F08.P2.justification: The unchanged canonical task explicitly makes a local b == 0 guard preference rung (ii). The retained guard therefore delivers every numbered requirement and is FULL, not a P-a substitution.

F09.P1.justification: std.mem.eql(u8, s1, s2) — documented contents comparison, unambiguously not identity comparison.

F09.P2.fragment:
std.sort.sort(i32, xs, {}, std.sort.desc(i32));
const lt = a < b;
F09.P2.justification: std.sort.sort/std.mem.sort with an explicit descending comparator function value sorts the slice in place (documented in-place mutation, no allocation).

F10.P1.fragment: const small: i32 = std.math.cast(i32, big) orelse 0;
F10.P1.justification: std.math.cast(i32, big) returns ?i32 (rung i, checked conversion yielding optional) — explicit, documented.

F10.P2.justification: Zig requires explicit @as(f64, i) / @floatFromInt(i) conversion before adding to a float; no implicit int-to-float promotion exists.

F11.P1.justification: xs[i] traps deterministically on out-of-range index under the frozen ReleaseSafe recipe (documented bounds-check behavior); std.mem provides no separate checked-optional indexed read as a competing form.

F11.P2.justification: xs[1..4] slice syntax shares storage with the original array/slice (documented non-copying view).

F12.P1.justification: var o: ?i32 = null; const n = o orelse 0; — optional type in the type signature and standard coalescing operator `orelse`.

F12.P2.justification: P-a: Zig's std library has no Optional.map/andThen chaining combinator; the canonical_task's non-if requirement can only be met by writing the explicit `if (o) |v| ... else null` unwrap form, the named R9 substitution.

F13.P1.fragment: fn parse_twice(s: []const u8) !i32 { const v = try std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10); return v * 2; }
F13.P1.justification: std.fmt.parseInt returns an error union (![]u8->!i32); `try` propagates the failure to the caller, and the function's own return type (!i32) documents fallibility.

F13.P2.fragment: const n: i32 = std.fmt.parseInt(i32, s, 10) catch 0;
F13.P2.justification: std.fmt.parseInt(...) catch 0; — standard local error-handling operator with an explicit fallback value.

F14.P1.fragment:
const Shape = union(enum) { Circle: struct{r:f64}, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} };
const s: Shape = .{.Circle = .{.r=2.0}};
F14.P1.justification: union(enum) { Circle: f64, Rect: struct{w:f64,h:f64} } is a closed, exhaustive tagged union; the compiler forbids adding a case elsewhere.

F14.P2.justification: switch (s) on the tagged union with no else arm is compiler-checked for exhaustiveness (compile error on missing case).

F14.P3.fragment: manual vtable pattern: shapes unit declares Shape interface struct with fn ptr; Circle/Rect implement it; separate unit adds Tri implementing the same shape; dispatch through function pointer.
F14.P3.justification: The current canonical task requires an extensible abstract operation across a separate unit; it does not require a built-in nominal interface keyword. Zig's documented type-erasure/vtable idiom using *anyopaque plus function pointers lets the shapes unit define the abstract Shape value while a separate unit adds Tri without editing shapes and dispatches area at runtime. All numbered requirements are therefore delivered without an R9 substitution.

F15.P1.justification: fn head(comptime T: type, xs: []const T) T { return xs[0]; } — declaration-level parametric type T with a statically recoverable T->T result relationship, reused at i32 and []const u8.

F15.P2.fragment: fn max_of(comptime T: type, a: T, b: T) T { return if (a > b) a else b; }
F15.P2.justification: P-a/P-c: Zig has no declaration-site trait/interface constraint syntax; a generic function's requirements are enforced only structurally at instantiation via comptime duck-typing, so misuse is diagnosed at the call/instantiation site, not at the generic's own declaration as the canonical_task requires.

F15.P3.fragment: manual vtable/fat-pointer pattern for Named interface with A/B implementations and a heterogeneous []Named-like slice of tagged pointers, dispatched at runtime.
F15.P3.justification: The current canonical task asks for one declared abstract element type that can hold A and B and dispatch tag at runtime; it does not require a built-in interface construct. A Zig type-erased Named value with *anyopaque context plus a tag function pointer is one declared element type, can populate a heterogeneous sequence, and dispatches to the concrete implementation. The legacy PARTIAL/P-a classification therefore treated the ordinary vtable idiom as a substitute when it actually satisfies every numbered requirement.

F16.P1.justification: std.ArrayList(i32) literal-style init plus a for-loop summing elements (no single-call fold/sum combinator in std, so the explicit iteration form is the R10-selected minimal form).

F16.P2.justification: std.StringHashMap(i32) with an iterator for entries, and .get("b") orelse 0 for the missing-key fallback lookup.

F17.P1.fragment: fn read_all() !usize { const file = try std.fs.cwd().openFile("data.txt", .{}); defer file.close(); const text = try file.readToEndAlloc(allocator, 1<<20); return text.len; }
F17.P1.justification: defer file.close(); immediately after a successful open guarantees release on every exit path including the failure path of the subsequent read, per Zig's documented defer semantics (always runs at scope exit, LIFO).

F17.P2.justification: P-a: Zig has no automatic end-of-lifetime hook (no destructors/drop); a user type's cleanup (incrementing `released`) must be invoked explicitly via `defer h.deinit();` at the call site rather than triggered automatically by the language at scope exit, the named R9-style substitution for a deterministic destructor.

F18.P1.justification: const std = @import("std"); std.debug.print("x\n", .{}); — import introduces `std` into scope, output statement is standard.

F18.P2.fragment:
util.zig: pub fn pub_add(a:i32,b:i32) i32 { return a+b+secret(); } fn secret() i32 { return 1; }
main: util.pub_add(2,3)
F18.P2.justification: `pub fn pub_add` vs a non-`pub` `fn secret` in a `util.zig` module/file; `secret` is compiler-enforced unreachable outside the file; external call via `util.pub_add(2,3)` after `@import("util.zig")`, using the frozen multi-unit recipe.

F19.P1.fragment: two std.Thread.spawn calls computing 20 and 22 into pointers, t1.join(); t2.join(); return sum.
F19.P1.justification: std.Thread.spawn for two threads computing 20 and 22, .join() on both, summing results — Zig's current (post-async-removal) standard concurrency facility is OS threads via std.Thread, which is a standard, toolchain-shipped mechanism.

F19.P2.fragment: std.atomic.Value(i64) counter; two std.Thread.spawn workers each looping fetchAdd(1,.SeqCst) 1000 times; join both; return counter.load(.SeqCst).
F19.P2.justification: std.Thread.Mutex guarding the shared i64 counter across two threads each incrementing 1000 times, joined before reading the final value — documented race-free discipline via an explicit lock, verifiable in principle by repeated runs.

F20.P1.justification: extern fn abs(x: c_int) c_int; declared and linked against libc per the frozen recipe (Zig's built-in C FFI, no third-party binding generator).

F20.P2.fragment: export fn add2(a: i32, b: i32) callconv(.C) i32 { return a + b; }
F20.P2.justification: export fn add2(a: c_int, b: c_int) c_int { return a + b; } — Zig's `export` keyword produces a C-ABI, unmangled external symbol directly, per language documentation.
